# CI performance

The successful main run [37125016168](https://github.com/DidYouStudy/App/actions/runs/37125016168)
(2026-10-03, commit `37915ac`) spent 10m34s in its single CI job:

| Step | Duration |
| --- | --- |
| Gradle cache restore | 12s |
| Create uncached AVD snapshot | 1m53s |
| Formatting | 45s |
| Assemble and lint | 3m15s |
| Unit tests/check | 25s |
| Connected tests | 2m35s |
| Coverage and Sonar upload | 41s |
| Cache uploads | 39s |

## Workflow

- Build, lint, formatting and unit tests run in one Gradle invocation. Debug
  **and release** assembly remain required.
- Android tests run on a separate runner alongside the build checks. APKs are
  prepared before starting the emulator; the test command reuses those outputs.
- Sonar runs after both jobs. Build bytecode, unit execution data, lint/JUnit
  reports and connected execution data are transferred as one-day artifacts.
  Its JaCoCo task combines unit and connected coverage without rerunning unit
  tests. Full Git history is fetched only for change detection and Sonar.
- AVD snapshots are already cached by the old workflow. The new key includes
  runner OS/architecture and image identity. Bump its version when an emulator
  upgrade invalidates snapshots. The first run with a new key is slower.
- Build checks use configuration caching. To reuse it **between runs**, add a
  repository Actions secret named `GRADLE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` containing an AES key
  (for example generated by `openssl rand -base64 16`). Without it, builds still
  run, and Gradle's normal build/dependency cache remains enabled.
- Superseded PR runs are cancelled. Main runs finish to populate shared caches.

The required status check keeps the name `CI`. It succeeds only when all three
Android jobs succeed, or when a successfully classified documentation-only
change skips all three. Routing unit tests run on every invocation, require at
least 90% Python coverage, and transfer their XML report to Sonar alongside
the Android coverage.
Only root Markdown files and Markdown under `docs/` are documentation-only;
assets, resources, scripts, dependency files and unknown paths run full CI.
Missing comparison commits also run full CI. Renames are compared as deletion
and addition so moving code into documentation cannot bypass checks.

## Measuring the result

Compare runs with matching cache conditions (especially the AVD cache-hit
output). Measure event-to-`CI` completion, including job queues and cache uploads,
and compare several warm runs rather than a single cold run. The desired 3–4
minute target is a hypothesis until GitHub-hosted runs confirm it. Parallel jobs
can increase total runner minutes even while reducing elapsed time.

Possible follow-ups if the warm critical path remains too long:

1. Inspect release R8 timings; consider a separate release validation policy
   only with team agreement, since removing PR release assembly reduces coverage.
2. Inspect emulator boot versus APK compile/install/test time before sharding
   tests. The current test suite is small, so more runners may add overhead.
3. Validate configuration-cache compatibility separately for connected testing
   and Sonar before enabling it on those commands.

References:
[Gradle action caching](https://github.com/gradle/actions/blob/main/docs/setup-gradle.md),
[AVD snapshot caching](https://github.com/ReactiveCircus/android-emulator-runner),
[GitHub required checks and filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax).
